syntax.rationale: The syntax section documents the declaration surface: writing multiple @container conditions in a single rule separated by commas, including examples of targeting the same container with OR semantics and targeting different named containers in the same comma list.

inputs.rationale: The inputs to the comma-separated container query rule are the comma-delimited container conditions in the @container prelude, each specifying an optional container name and query condition (size or style feature query).

outputs.rationale: The output/evaluation effect is conditional application of the enclosed style rules when any one of the comma-separated conditions matches, implementing logical OR semantics across independent container queries.

errors.rationale: CSS container queries have no script-facing error or exception surface: malformed query syntax or unsupported conditions are handled per standard CSS parser error-handling rules by invalidating or dropping the query condition without throwing.

context.rationale: The context is CSS stylesheet rules where @container conditional group rules evaluate container context for descendant elements based on named or nearest container features.

lifecycle.rationale: Container queries participate in the browser layout and style recalculation lifecycle with no script-facing lifecycle events, initialization steps, or teardown requirements.

examples.rationale: A complete <pre><code> example showing a comma-separated container query providing a scroll-state() query with a width query fallback for sticky header positioning.

compatibility.rationale: Browser support table listing Chrome (149 developer trial), Edge (149), Firefox (Shipped), and Safari.

securityPrivacy.rationale: Comma-separated container queries inspect same-document container layout and style state without accessing cross-origin data, persistent storage, user identity, or device sensors.
